name: Muskegon Woman's Club
description:
Muskegon Woman's Club
The Muskegon Woman’s Club was founded in 1890 and dedicated to the intellectual “improvement and development” of women. The Chicago firm of Weir and Perry designed this Neoclassical structure, built in 1902 with funds donated by Minnie Smith, the widow of Muskegon attorney Francis Smith. The club lobbied the city to hire the first police woman, held performances, and worked with charitable groups such as the Red Cross and the Council of National Defense.

The Muskegon Woman’s Club was founded in 1890 and dedicated to the intellectual “improvement and development” of women. The Chicago firm of Weir and Perry designed this Neoclassical structure, built in 1902 with funds donated by Minnie Smith, the widow of Muskegon attorney Francis Smith. The club lobbied the city to hire the first police woman, held performances, and worked with charitable groups such as the Red Cross and the Council of National Defense.
